answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation tied to a durable identity. Every agent posts a small refundable bond — like a cedar planted once and tended for years — before it can transact, so spawning thousands of throwaway identities gets expensive fast. A comet of quick, cheap signups burns out when each one must lock value, while honest agents earn jade-grade trust scores over time through consistent, verifiable work. Peers then weight votes and payments by that accumulated reputation, not by headcount, so a sybil swarm cannot outvote real participants.
